title: A 200-year-old kalgi and a 30-carat emerald necklace: what Kareena Kapoor Khan wore this Diwali

 Open Navigation Menu Menu Trends A 200-year-old kalgi and a 30-carat emerald necklace: what Kareena Kapoor Khan wore this Diwali
 The actor accessorised her Punit Balana kaftan with heirloom jewellery from the Nawab and Begum of Bhopal By Vogue Staff 11 November 2026 Instagram.com/rheakapoor Kareena Kapoor Khan’s jewellery stole the show at Diwali . The actor, whose personal style lies at the intersection of comfort and chicness, chose a kaftan look from the Jaipur-based designer Punit Balana, but proved that an oversized silhouette—when accessorised with the right jewellery—can look not only elevated but also coveted.
 Instagram.com/rheakapoor The kaftan, designed in collaboration with Kapoor Khan's stylist Rhea Kapoor, itself was not an ordinary design. Balana turned the simplistic silhouette into a piece of art, showcasing one of Rajasthan’s most heritage craft techniques. Lappe ka kaam, commonly known as gota patti work, inundated the beige-coloured, floor-length breezy design. Originally made with real silver, the ‘gota’ or metallic ribbon is no longer made with the precious metal because of its rising cost. In Kapoor Khan’s piece, the appliqué embroidery technique was reimagined with silver, thereby reviving a heritage craft technique with a prowess that very few artisans possess. It showcased designs inspired by jali-like patterns, seen in the architecture of old forts and havelis of Rajasthan, crafted entirely by hand by piecing strips of silver gota.
 The kaftan embroidered with real silver became the perfect canvas for showcasing Kapoor Khan’s jewels, which were the pièces de résistance of her look. Kapoor Khan brought an androgynous slant to her look by wearing the dress with a turban, accessorised with a kalgi (or sarpench) that has been in Saif Ali Khan’s family for at least 200 years, and originally belonged to the Nawab of Bhopal. The three-pronged, diamond-encrusted design was worn by Ali Khan in 2012 as part of his groomswear attire for his wedding with Kapoor Khan.
 Instagram.com/rheakapoor The actor completed the look with her choker-style necklace and a diamond -encrusted chain from her family’s heirloom vault. The chain featured a 30-carat emerald stone, inscribed with Ayat-ul-Kursi—a powerful verse from the holy Quran. The jewellery belonged to his grandmother, Sajida Sultan, the daughter of Muhammad Hamidullah Khan, the last Nawab of Bhopal, before coming into Saif Ali Khan’s possession.
 Her makeup stayed neutral, complementary to the palette of the kaftan and the turban, while her hair was perfectly straightened and left open underneath it.
